answer: Each agent earns influence only after locking a scarce stake that can be slashed when its signed claims fail independent checks; splitting one identity into an ember, an island, and a sonnet of accounts does not multiply that stake. A Sybil attacker must therefore buy and lock more capital for each unit of voting weight, bear opportunity cost while it is unavailable, and risk losing it if fabricated reports are caught. This raises the attack’s cost rather than making fake identities impossible.
